The '''2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 19 August 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/1001/908864-gaa-season-2018/ |title=How the GAA season might look in 2018 following Special Congress vote|date=2 October 2017|work=RTE Sport|access-date=20 October 2017}}</ref> between [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|131st final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]].

Limerick won the match, ending a 45-year wait for a title.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/how-the-game-was-won-37231542.html |title =How the game was won|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/there-were-more-shots-than-hooks-blocks-and-tackles-five-talking-points-from-limericks-dramatic-allireland-triumph-37230764.html|title =There were more shots than hooks, blocks and tackles - Five talking points from Limerick's dramatic All-Ireland triumph|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/martin-breheny-allireland-final-match-report-limericks-new-wave-swamp-sloppy-tribe-37231548.html |title =Martin Breheny All-Ireland final match report: Limerick's new wave swamp sloppy Tribe|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-win-first-all-ireland-hurling-title-in-45-years-863141.html |title =Limerick win first All Ireland hurling title in 45 years|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986137-is-limericks-road-to-glory-the-most-impressive-ever/ |title =Is Limerick's road to All-Ireland glory the most impressive ever?|date=20 August 2018|work=RTE News|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limericks-dreams-becomes-one-of-the-gaas-greatest-sporting-moments-863795.html|title =Limerick's 'Dreams' becomes one of the GAA's greatest sporting moments|date=22 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	

The final was shown live in Ireland on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' live programme, presented by [[Michael Lyster]] from Croke Park, with studio analysis from [[Liam Sheedy]], [[Henry Shefflin]] and [[Ger Loughnane]]. Match commentary was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] with analysis by [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The game was also shown live on [[Sky Sports]], presented by [[Rachel Wyse]] and [[Brian Carney (rugby)|Brian Carney]].
		
The match drew a peak audience of more than 1 million on RTÉ. The TV audience for ''The Sunday Game'' coverage peaked at 1,007,500 by the end of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/330764/1-000-000-tv-viewers-for-limerick-s-all-ireland-final-win.html |title =More than a million TV viewers for Limericks All Ireland Win|date=20 August 2018|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0820/986301-huge-numbers-tune-in-to-watch-limerick-end-45-year-wait/ |title =Huge numbers tune in to watch Limerick end 45-year wait for Liam MacCarthy success|date=20 August 2018|work=RTE News|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Background==
Galway were the defending champions and were looking to win their sixth [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland title]] after winning in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1923]], [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1980]], [[1987 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1987]], [[1988 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1988]], and [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2017]].
Limerick were appearing in their first final since [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2007]] and were looking for an eighth title after winning in [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1897]], [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1918]], [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1921]], [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1934]], [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1936]], [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1940]], and [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1973]].
The two counties had played each other in the final twice prior to this: in [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1923]] and [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1980]] with Galway winning both.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/sean-silke-4am-wake-up-gearbag-missing-and-happy-limerick-fans-at-the-door-862259.html |title = Sean Silke: 4am wake-up, gearbag missing, and happy Limerick fans at the door|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=15 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/2018-hurling-final/galway-probable-line-up-for-the-all-ireland-hurling-final-1.3594891 |title =Galway: probable line-up for the All-Ireland hurling final|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0815/985359-from-1973-to-now-limericks-long-wait-for-glory/ |title =From 1973 to now: Limerick's long wait for glory|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
===Build-up===
The final was shown on a giant screen at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd of 20,000 watched the match. A big screen was also in place in [[Eyre Square]] in Galway for the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/gaelic-grounds-limerick-bog-screen-hurling-final-galway-4171195-Aug2018/ |title =Gaelic Grounds to show Limerick-Galway All-Ireland hurling final on giant screen|date=9 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=9 August 2018}}</ref>

===Hurling stars of the 1990s===
The [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] team that won the [[1992 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1992 All-Ireland Final]] were honoured in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]] and as Kilkenny also won the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993 All-Ireland Final]] the GAA decided instead to honour the star hurlers of the 1990s. A group of senior GAA correspondents under the chairmanship of GAA President [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] selected the team. The team was presented to the crowd after the completion of the minor final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/gaa-hurling-stars-1990s-4182781-Aug2018/ |title =8 counties included as GAA to honour hurling stars of the 90s on All-Ireland final day|date=15 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/gaa-to-honour-hurling-team-of-the-1990s-at-allireland-final-and-some-big-names-have-been-left-out-37219723.html |title =GAA to honour 'Hurling Team of the 1990s' at All-Ireland final - and some big names have been left out|date=15 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=16 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaa.ie/hurling/news/gaa-confirms-ceremonies-and-events-around-the-all-ireland-hurling-finals/ |title = GAA has confirmed a list of events and ceremonies which will take place around this Sunday's All-Ireland hurling finals|date=17 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaa.ie/news-archive/news/hurling-heroes-of-the-1990s-to-be-honoured-on-all-ireland-final-sunday/ |title = GAA to salute the star hurlers of the 1990s |date=15 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref>

===Ticketing===
With a stadium capacity of 82,300, the 32 individual [[Gaelic Athletic Association county|county boards]] received 60,000 tickets. Schools and third level colleges got 2,500 tickets, while season ticket holders were entitled to 5,500 tickets. 1,000 tickets were given to overseas clubs. The [[Camogie Association|Camogie]], [[Ladies' Gaelic Football Association|Ladies' Football]], Handball and Rounders Associations were each allocated about 200 tickets, as were the jubilee teams and mini-7s which play at half-time. Demand for tickets was very high in both counties with Galway and Limerick having receiving around 32,000 tickets between. Stand tickets were priced at €80 with terrace at €40.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/brendan-cummins-hype-and-ticket-demands-are-part-of-the-final-buildup-but-opposition-should-be-first-concern-37198660.html |title = Brendan Cummins: Hype and ticket demands are part of the final build-up but opposition should be first concern|date=10 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=10 August 2018}}</ref>

==Match summary==
===Officials===
On 7 August 2018 the officials were chosen for the final by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]], with Wexford's [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] being named as the referee in what was his second senior final after being the referee in [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2015]]. Tipperary's [[Fergal Horgan]] was the standby referee with Kilkenny's Sean Cleere the linesman and Carlow's Patrick Murphy the sideline official.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/james-owens-wexford-referee-hurling-final-4168542-Aug2018/ |title = Wexford's Owens to take charge of Limerick-Galway All-Ireland hurling final|date=7 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref>

===Team news===
The Limerick team announced for the final was unchanged from the semi-final win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]]. Galway made one change to the starting team with [[Gearóid McInerney]] recovering from a calf injury he picked up in the drawn game against [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and coming in to replace [[Niall Burke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0817/985854-galway-limerick-teams/ |title = GAA teams: One switch for Galway, Limerick unchanged|date=18 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-3-16-galway-2-18-how-the-limerick-players-rated-1.3601266|title =Limerick 3-16 Galway 2-18: How the Limerick players rated|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>

===Summary===
Playing into the Davin end, [[Aaron Gillane]] opened the scoring for Limerick after 2 minutes. [[Joe Canning]] opened Galway's account with a 65 after 7 minutes to make the score 3 points to 1. Canning got another point in the 15th minute to level the score at 5 points each. In the 16th minute [[Graeme Mulcahy]] scrambled the ball over the line on the ground from close range after dropping it for the opening goal to put Limerick into a 2-point lead. A [[Séamus Flanagan]] point in the last minute of the first half made the score 1–10 to 0–9 at half-time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-316-galway-218-as-it-happened-the-45year-wait-for-the-treaty-men-is-over-37230279.html |title =2018 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	

Four minutes into the second-half Kyle Hayes got the opening score to increase the lead to 4 points. Kyle Hayes got the decision from Hawk-Eye with another point a minute later to increase the lead to 6 points. After 54 minutes, Limerick got their second goal when [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] pounced on a mistake from [[Gearoid McInerney]] to run in on goal and finish low and powerful to the net off the Hurley from the middle of the goal to put 9 points between the sides.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/all-ireland-shc-final/|title =Limerick win first All-Ireland SHC since 1973|date=19 August 2018|work=GAA.ie|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
In the 68th minute, substitute [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] got another goal for Limerick when he picked the ball up and finished with a low shot to the right of the net from the left to increase the lead to 8 points.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-3-16-galway-2-18-five-match-defining-moments-1.3601209|title =Limerick 3-16 Galway 2-18: Five match defining moments|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
 
In the first of the 8 minutes of added time Galway scored a goal when [[Conor Whelan]] shot powerfully to the right of the net, four minutes later [[Joe Canning]] got another goal with a powerful shot to the top left corner of the net from a free to put 2 points between the sides.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-galway-hurling-final-analysis-4193041-Aug2018/ |title =Analysis: Limerick dominate puck-outs, their ferocious work-rate and Galway's attacking woes|date=21 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
A minute later [[Niall Burke]] scored a point to put only one point between the sides. [[Graeme Mulcahy]] then scored a point for Limerick with a shot from the right to put 2 between them again before Joe Canning scored with a 65 to again make it a one-point game.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-hold-on-to-dethrone-galway-and-end-45-years-of-hurt-1.3601179|title =Limerick hold on to dethrone Galway and end 45 years of hurt|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>	
In the last minute of time added on, Galway were awarded a free form inside their own half on the right, Joe Canning took the free which dropped short and was eventually cleared before the final sounded with Limerick the winners by one point.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/galway-limerick-all-ireland-final-4189637-Aug2018/ |title =2018 All Ireland Final: as it happened|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/joe-cannings-all-ireland-final-free-wasnt-outside-his-range-it-was-just-probably-outside-his-comfort-zone-says-brother-ollie-882159.html |title =Joe Canning's All-Ireland final free 'wasn't outside his range, it was just probably outside his comfort zone', says brother Ollie|date=31 October 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 November 2018}}</ref>

===Trophy presentation===
Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]] accepted the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] from GAA president [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] in the Hogan Stand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-all-ireland-hurling-champions-4189777-Aug2018/ |title =Champs at last! Limerick end 45-year wait for All-Ireland hurling glory|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/billy-keane-hannon-raises-liam-to-lift-the-weight-of-45-years-off-a-countys-shoulders-37231486.html |title =Billy Keane: Hannon raises Liam to lift the weight of 45 years off a county's shoulders|date=19 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

===Reaction===
Speaking after the final whistle, Limerick manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] was happy that Limerick had held on in the final few minutes saying "It's huge, huge, huge relief, this group has phenomenal belief in its own abilities, its own resolve, that never-say-die attitude. We have worked so, so hard. Galway pushed us so hard in the last 10, 15 minutes. It was really difficult on the lads to hold their nerve to try and find those last few vital scores, but they did."<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986120-kiely-limerick-no-longer-second-class-hurling-citizens/|title =Kiely: Limerick no longer second-class hurling citizens|date=19 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/while-some-urge-limerick-fans-to-go-mental-john-kiely-yearns-for-somewhere-nice-and-quiet-863222.html |title =While some urge Limerick fans to 'go mental', John Kiely yearns for 'somewhere nice and quiet'|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/330636/bridesmaid-no-more-declares-victorious-limerick-hurling-manager-john-kiely.html |title ='Bridesmaid no more' declares victorious Limerick hurling manager John Kiely|date=20 August 2018|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>

Galway manager [[Micheál Donoghue]] accepted that his side were 'a tad off' in the final but vowed that they will be back again next year saying "We're bitterly disappointed. I just felt we probably didn't get into the game but you have to give huge credit to Limerick. They started really well and were dominant for long periods."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986129-we-were-a-tad-off-but-these-boys-will-be-back/ |title =Donoghue: We were a tad off but these boys will be back|date=19 August 2018|work=RTE Sport|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/these-boys-have-shown-massive-resilience-theyll-be-back-micheal-donoghue-37236021.html |title =These boys have shown massive resilience, they'll be back - Micheal Donoghue|date=21 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=23 August 2018}}</ref>		
		
Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ2]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Eddie Brennan]], and [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Kyle Hayes]], [[Declan Hannon]] and [[Joe Canning]] with Kyle Hayes winning the award which was presented by GAA president [[John Horan (GAA President)|John Horan]] at the City West hotel in Dublin where the post match Limerick function was being held.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kyle-hayes-man-of-the-match-4190424-Aug2018/ |title =Limerick's Kyle Hayes named All-Ireland final man of the match|date=19 August 2018|work=The 42|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kyle-hayes-wins-man-of-the-match-limerick-dominate-sunday-game-best-xv-but-galway-star-was-their-hurler-of-the-year-37231272.html |title =Kyle Hayes wins Man of the Match, Limerick dominate Sunday Game best XV but Galway star was their hurler of the year|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>
